articles.title: EvoBelief: Falsifiable World Models for Self-Improving LLM Agents
articles.summary: The paper introduces EvoBelief, a self-evolving world model for LLM agents that updates environment knowledge through falsifiable hypotheses rather than changing model parameters. It reports improved benchmark performance across tasks involving static dynamics, hidden drift, and scientific discovery, including better recovery after environment changes and stronger results in DiscoveryWorld's Reactor Lab.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is an early research signal for more reliable AI agents that can adapt to changing environments, validate assumptions, and link decisions to evidence. While not directly investable, it points toward future enterprise agent architectures where governance, auditability, and workflow reliability become important differentiators.

articles.title: DeltaLLM: Delta-Key Sparse Attention for Edge LLMs
articles.summary: DeltaLLM is a training-free framework designed to accelerate on-device LLM prefilling attention for edge platforms, where compute and memory constraints make long prompts difficult to process. The paper reports up to 60% Delta-Key sparsity, 63% structured attention-score sparsity, negligible average accuracy loss, and a 1.62x speedup on a KV260 FPGA board versus TeLLMe-v2 while reducing DSP and BRAM usage.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is a technical but relevant signal that AI infrastructure innovation is extending beyond cloud GPUs toward edge devices and specialized hardware. If approaches like this prove practical, they could support broader on-device LLM deployment by lowering latency, memory use, and hardware resource requirements, with potential read-throughs for edge AI hardware, embedded systems, and efficient inference software ecosystems.
